common:
Work in [PROJECT_PATH], an existing project folder in one of the /data/ai/projects groups: [PROJECT_GROUPS]. Replace every [PLACEHOLDER] before starting. Keep files and operational state within this project: .opencode/work, .opencode/validation and .opencode/captures. Register captures with the maintained project capture command so they appear under /data/ai/captures; do not create project aliases or compatibility symlinks.

Conserve tokens: use narrow reads, installed skills and actual tool schemas, stable job IDs and durable receipts. Reconcile existing jobs before another submission. Follow current serial handoff/vision rules; resume only exact returned agent/sessionID pairs. Never fabricate evidence, delete guards or repeat an unchanged rejected call. Respect exclusive GPU ownership and active jobs. Report PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT TESTED from actual results.

templates.title: Build a Blender game asset
templates.prompt: Create [ASSET_DESCRIPTION] using watoom-blender-asset-builder with dimensions [DIMENSIONS], target [TARGET_ENGINE] and budget [POLYGON_BUDGET]. Use semantic named parts and materials, a dimension/contact plan and an empty scene. Preserve versioned source, run the request checkpoints including mandatory final packed-source QA, real engine validation and actual multi-view image review. Use the Prompt Builder page for guided questions and safe defaults.

templates.title: Find assets for a project
templates.prompt: Find suitable existing assets for [ASSET_DESCRIPTION]. Search the shared asset Catalog first using the installed asset.search route. Return a short ranked list with asset IDs, formats, dependencies, licence/source and actual compatibility evidence. Inspect only selected candidates. Do not download or copy whole packs.

templates.title: Index selected downloaded assets
templates.prompt: Index the receipt-verified files in [SOURCE_DIRECTORY] using the existing asset.index route and shared Catalog. Reuse existing IDs/adapters, preserve prior records and verify a subsequent search. Exclude incomplete downloads and unsupported formats; do not create another Catalog.

templates.title: Acquire owned FAB assets
templates.prompt: Check my existing server-authenticated FAB library for [ASSET_NAME]. Reconcile acquisition receipts before downloading. Use the maintained single-owner queue with hashes and resource bounds; never duplicate a downloader or re-download PASS assets. Index only verified complete files into the shared Catalog. Separate downloaded, indexed and runtime-compatible states. Do not purchase anything or expose account credentials. If host acquisition is unavailable to this session, report the precise missing capability once.

templates.title: Inspect a mesh
templates.prompt: Inspect the indexed asset [ASSET_ID] through the installed asset.inspect or mesh-inspection route. Report topology, finite bounds, scale, pivot, normals, UV/material slots and collision/rig information actually verified. Produce a project-local preview and inspect its pixels. Preserve the source.

templates.title: Optimise an asset
templates.prompt: Prepare an optimised copy of indexed asset [ASSET_ID] for [TARGET_ENGINE], targeting [POLYGON_BUDGET] triangles and [TEXTURE_BUDGET]. Use asset.optimize after inspecting its installed schema. Preserve source materials/UVs and record before/after counts, bounds and visual differences. Import and validate the output before calling it game-ready.

templates.title: Repair and export a mesh
templates.prompt: Repair [PROJECT_MESH_FILE] using the installed mesh-repair/export route. Fix only confirmed geometry defects, preserve an original copy and record changes. Validate topology, normals, UVs, scale and exported geometry; compare actual before/after previews. Do not claim automatic rigging or animation.

templates.title: Generate a prototype with LLaMA-Mesh
templates.prompt: Generate one simple [OBJECT_DESCRIPTION] prototype with the existing synchronous watoom-llama-mesh MCP generate tool. Discover its actual arguments and use one stable request ID. Let the existing GPU controller own switching/restoration; never direct-scale models. Validate output geometry, then use Blender cleanup, sensible scale/pivot and an actual preview. Keep raw, cleaned and game-ready stages distinct. This is a prototype; do not claim textures, rigging or production quality without evidence.

templates.title: Generate a procedural asset on CPU
templates.prompt: Generate [ASSET_DESCRIPTION] with the installed typed CPU procedural generator registry: avian, quadruped, human, tree, terrain, building or rock. Discover the actual generator ID, bounded parameters and output contract before using the native 3D route. Use only the requested supported generator; do not execute downloaded code or substitute LLaMA-Mesh inference. Validate scale, geometry and export, and inspect the produced views. If rigging/animation is provided, verify actual motion and engine import before acceptance.

templates.title: Derive a material
templates.prompt: Use material.derive for indexed source [ASSET_ID] to prepare [MATERIAL_DESCRIPTION] for [TARGET_ENGINE]. Inspect supported fields and output maps first. Verify map roles, colour spaces, dimensions and material assignment, then inspect an actual rendered surface. Do not invent missing PBR channels or claim shader fidelity from texture files alone.

templates.title: Prepare a character
templates.prompt: Use character.prepare for indexed character [ASSET_ID] and target [TARGET_ENGINE]. Inspect the installed requirements for skeleton/animations before running. Preserve hierarchy, scale, materials and existing clips. Validate actual Idle/Walk/Run motion where supplied, check two times per clip and review captures. Report missing rigging or animation rather than claiming it was created.

templates.title: Create a procedural dungeon
templates.prompt: Create a small editable Unreal dungeon for [DUNGEON_DESCRIPTION], using [BUILDER_OR_FORGE_OR_MIXED], [ROOM_COUNT] rooms, [LEVEL_COUNT] levels and seed [SEED]. Search the shared Catalog for a verified adapter, inspect the installed world.compose schema and submit one stable job ID. Reconcile the job before retrying. Require native floor/wall/capsule checks and Recast connectivity including stairs, editable-map reopening and actual textured previews. Procedural generation is not an exact source-map replica.

templates.title: Recreate a supplied map
templates.prompt: Recreate [SOURCE_MAP_IMAGE] as a small editable Unreal dungeon with [COLUMNS] columns, [ROWS] rows and [CELL_SIZE_CM] cm cells. Derive walkable cells, blocked cells, internal wall edges and doors from actual pixel review; state uncertainties and validate bounds/connectivity. Discover whether fixed_layout is supported by the installed pipeline. Never submit a seeded world as an exact replica. If no supported fixed-layout/project assembly route exists, report the exact capability gap once. Use a fresh output for a changed plan; never delete identity guards. Deliver the editable project plus real overhead/perspective Unreal captures. No gameplay or additional systems.

templates.title: Start an offline Hyper project
templates.prompt: Stage a NEW offline Hyper Combat project from the verified complete source, preserving its /Game/Hyper namespace, Config and input. Use the maintained unreal-project IaC path; do not overwrite an existing project or treat mesh world.compose as complete-framework staging. The accepted test uses offline Engine.GameInstance. Do not assume BP_GameInstance_Base or online multiplayer support; HOI/provider setup is a separate project-specific task. Validate project load and applicable Blueprint/gameplay checks before claiming the new project works. If this session lacks host staging access, report that boundary once.

templates.title: Unreal static assets to Godot
templates.prompt: Convert selected Unreal asset/map [ASSET_OR_MAP] into static geometry for Godot. Preserve the authored /Game dependency namespaces, use the accepted native Unreal route to bake/finalise geometry, export via GLTFExporter to GLB, then import into Godot. Check finite geometry, scale, textures/materials, colliders and actual captures. Unreal Blueprints, plugin logic and GeometryCache effects do not automatically transfer through GLB.

templates.title: Assess an Unreal plugin or integration kit
templates.prompt: Assess [PLUGIN_OR_ARCHIVE] for [PROJECT_AND_ENGINE_VERSION]. Inspect its descriptor, source documentation, licence, platform allowlist, dependencies and binary/build IDs without executing downloaded code or auto-connecting MCP. Nwiro/POT Linux support and arbitrary engine-version compatibility must not be assumed. Identify a supported isolated qualification/build route; preserve the accepted engine and existing project. Only enable the integration after actual load, relevant behaviour and rollback validation. If no supported route exists, report the exact boundary and keep the integration disabled.

templates.title: Blender assets or animation to Godot
templates.prompt: Prepare [BLEND_OR_MESH_FILE] for Godot using the installed Blender route. Export only required runtime meshes/armatures, preserve materials and bake evaluated animation where appropriate. Validate GLB structure and finite values, import into Godot and check collisions/scale. For animation, verify source motion and imported motion at two distinct times, then inspect real captures.

templates.title: Small native Godot prototype
templates.prompt: Build a small Godot proof of concept for [IDEA] in this project. Inspect existing code and installed Godot version first; reuse suitable indexed portable assets. Implement only [MINIMUM_SCOPE]. Run meaningful headless import/tests and actual visual checks. Keep generated output project-local and preserve unrelated gameplay. Deliver opening/running instructions, captures and honest remaining limitations.

templates.title: Capture an existing Unreal or Godot project
templates.prompt: Capture the existing [ENGINE] project/map [PROJECT_OR_MAP] without rebuilding its content. Discover the supported capture route and use legitimate GPU ownership/admission. Container /dev/dri absence does not establish that the host lacks NVIDIA hardware. Produce a useful overhead and perspective capture after shader/texture loading and UI repaint. Review actual pixels for framing, lighting, missing assets and dialogs. Nonblack PNG statistics are not visual acceptance.

templates.title: Validate an Unreal effect such as BloodFX
templates.prompt: Validate selected effect [EFFECT_ASSET] in an isolated project using the accepted Unreal runtime and supported fenced rendering. Preserve the source. Prove actual animation at multiple times, visible motion and material/render fidelity with captures. Static load, timeline metadata and successful export are not playback evidence. If portable Godot output is requested, inspect an explicitly supported bake/conversion route and prove imported motion separately; GLTF static export does not convert GeometryCache or Niagara logic.

templates.title: Generate an image with an installed model
templates.prompt: Generate [IMAGE_DESCRIPTION] using installed managed image model [MODEL_OR_INSTALLATION_ID]. Discover the current generation interface and published sampling recommendations. For a LoRA, select an explicit compatible installed base. Use the existing GPU controller; preserve active jobs and verify primary restoration. Save the output and generation settings under this project, inspect the actual image and report limitations honestly.

templates.title: Download and register a model
templates.prompt: Set up [HUGGING_FACE_REPOSITORY_URL] through the existing Model Manager at https://glance.internal.homelab.example/model-manager/. Inspect revisions, exact variant sizes, model type and dependency requirements. Distinguish GGUF, diffusion checkpoint/pipeline and LoRA. Use safe applicable settings (100000 context,4096 output,q4_0 K/V for compatible language models; lower model limits take precedence), preserving explicit saved overrides. Report downloaded/configured/registered/tested separately. No arbitrary remote-code execution, direct scaling or deletion of existing data.

templates.title: Research with SearXNG
templates.prompt: Research [QUESTION] using the configured web-search/SearXNG tools. Inspect available tools rather than guessing endpoints. Prefer primary sources, cite links next to findings, distinguish verified facts from inference and save a short sourced report. Keep searches bounded and avoid fetching unrelated pages.

templates.title: Creative writing
templates.prompt: Write [FORMAT] about [PREMISE], approximately [LENGTH], in [TONE] for [AUDIENCE]. Use the selectable creativewriter agent and relevant installed English writing/world-building skills. Preserve supplied canon, state only critical assumptions and produce the requested writing rather than a long plan. Save the draft and any continuity notes in this project.

templates.title: Authorised native Kali tools
templates.prompt: Perform an authorised security check of [EXPLICIT_OWNED_TARGET] limited to [SCOPE_AND_ALLOWED_TESTS]. Discover the installed native Kali tool interface and execute through the configured route from WatooM Code. Do not invent shell flags or endpoints, broaden scope, change networking or expose credentials. Keep a concise command/result record and evidence-backed findings. Ask before any destructive action or action outside the stated scope.

templates.title: Implement and test a change
templates.prompt: Implement [CHANGE] in this project. Inspect existing source/tests and choose the smallest correct change. Follow installed role/handoff rules with exact agent/session pairs and no duplicate modifying children. Run meaningful affected tests, check actual behaviour and preserve unrelated changes. Keep durable infrastructure changes in authoritative IaC; report the commit, validation and remaining blockers.

templates.title: Maintain and activate an IaC fix
templates.prompt: Fix [OBSERVED_ISSUE] through the authoritative homelab IaC repository. Collect narrow read-only evidence first, preserve unrelated changes and prepare the exact change/snapshot/rollback. Validate affected source and activate within existing approval and ownership rules. Wait for active work to settle rather than forcing scaling or killing jobs. Verify live behaviour and persist the fix in the normal build path. No network/firewall/DNS/driver changes unless explicitly requested.

templates.title: Game from a genre template
templates.prompt: Start a Godot game for [IDEA] from an installed, licence-checked genre template. Search the game template catalogue (platformer, metroidvania, deckbuilder, tower defense, RTS, top-down shooter, FPS/TPS, racing, souls-like, RPG, starter) and name the best match with its licence, pinned revision and declared Godot version; if none fits, say so rather than forcing one. Copy it into this project, never edit the library copy. Check it imports under the installed Godot, then implement only [MINIMUM_SCOPE] on top of it. Run headless import/tests and real captures. Keep attribution and licence files. Report what came from the template, what you changed and honest limitations.

templates.title: Full game from a design interview
templates.prompt: Build [GAME] end to end using the game-development blueprint. Run the design intake interview first, then write a milestone plan of small bounded tasks sized for the local models, routing each task to the matching WatooM pipeline, asset flow or genre template. After every milestone run the critique, performance and code-design gate before continuing. Keep output project-local, record checkpoints, and stop for owner input where the interview left a decision open.

templates.title: Real-world terrain to Godot
templates.prompt: Turn the real-world location [PLACE_OR_LAT_LONG] into a Godot terrain for [USE]. Follow the terrain-map pipeline: resolve the area and extent, fetch elevation data, build the heightmap and mesh, import into Godot and use height_at() for placement. State the data source, resolution, licence and vertical exaggeration. Verify the mesh is not inverted and take real captures. Keep output project-local and report limitations.
